context:
Patient: 59F, breast cancer survivor (2016: dose-dense AC, cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast RT, on anastrozole), presents with left axillary mass, fevers to 38.4 C, drenching night sweats; ECOG 1, LDH 510. Non-GCB DLBCL (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%, FISH negative for rearrangements), PET nodes above and below the diaphragm plus splenic nodules, marrow negative, and new LVEF 45% (62% in 2016) with GLS -14%.
What this case tests: Spleen is a nodal site under Lugano, so stage is III, not IV, and IPI is 2. | Double-expressor by IHC but FISH-negative, so not double-hit; no intensification to DA-EPOCH-R. | Prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest RT and LVEF 62% to 45% mean standard full-dose R-CHOP / Pola-R-CHP is not safe as is. | Treatment must stay curative: anthracycline-free (R-CEOP / R-GCVP) or cardio-protected regimen, with cardio-oncology input and cardioprotective drugs. | CNS-IPI 2 with no high-risk sites: no routine CNS prophylaxis.

answer.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (WHO 2022 / ICC: DLBCL, NOS), non-germinal center (Hans non-GCB) phenotype, MYC and BCL2 double-expressor, with no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement on interphase FISH. This is not double-hit lymphoma and not high-grade B-cell lymphoma. Disease is nodal with splenic involvement and no identifiable extranodal primary. Carcinoma is excluded: AE1/AE3 and GATA3 are negative in the lesional cells and there is no epithelial morphology. The 2016 ER-positive left breast cancer is not recurrent: breast on PET is negative, and the 2026-03 mammogram was benign. The lymphoma is unrelated to the breast cancer and does not change its adjuvant plan.
answer.stage: Ann Arbor stage IIIB. Nodal disease is present above and below the diaphragm (left axillary, mediastinal, mesenteric, para-aortic), and the spleen has multiple FDG-avid nodules. Under Lugano the spleen is a lymphoid organ, so this is staged as nodal, not extranodal stage IV. If the splenic nodules were judged extranodal, the stage would be IV; management would not change. B symptoms are present (fever to 38.4 C, drenching night sweats). Weight loss is about 3%, which is below the 10% threshold. Bone marrow biopsy and PET are both negative. There is no liver, lung, bone, kidney or adrenal involvement. The largest mass is 7.5 cm (mesenteric), so it is not bulky by NCCN criteria (10 cm or more). IPI is 2 (low-intermediate): stage III and elevated LDH, with age 59, ECOG 1, albumin normal and no more than one extranodal site. Beta-2 microglobulin is 2.9 mg/L (high).
answer.biology: Non-GCB phenotype: CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 positive in about 80% of cells. Ki-67 is about 80%. MYC is expressed in 45% of cells and BCL2 in 70%, both above the conventional double-expressor cutoffs (MYC 40%, BCL2 50%). Interphase FISH on 200 nuclei shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement, so this is not double-hit. EBER is negative, CD30 is negative, CD5 and cyclin D1 are negative, and flow shows a kappa-restricted CD19+/CD20+ population. Double-expressor biology carries a worse outcome even with R-CHOP, and this does not by itself change the NCCN first-line choice. Optional genotyping (TP53, MYD88 L265P, CD79B) would refine prognosis but would not change the plan below.
answer.prognosis: Intermediate-risk by IPI but adverse by biology: non-GCB, double-expressor, LDH 2.3 times ULN, beta-2 microglobulin 2.9, B symptoms, and large abdominal and splenic disease. With full-dose R-CHOP-era therapy I would expect long-term progression-free survival in roughly the half-to-two-thirds range; double-expressor status pulls the estimate toward the lower end. An anthracycline-free regimen is probably less effective than R-CHOP, so the cure probability is lower than that, and I cannot quote a validated figure for this regimen. These are clinical estimates, not validated numbers. The main determinant of cure will be the early and end-of-treatment PET response.
answer.first_line_treatment: Anthracycline-free rituximab-based immunochemotherapy with curative intent: polatuzumab vedotin + rituximab + cyclophosphamide + prednisone (Pola-R-CP), every 21 days for 6 cycles. Doses per label and protocol: polatuzumab 1.8 mg/kg day 1 (weight 70 kg); rituximab 375 mg/m2 day 1; cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 day 1; prednisone 100 mg days 1-5 (BSA 1.79 m2). Pharmacy to verify. Reason for the choice: she has already received 240 mg/m2 doxorubicin, her LVEF has fallen from 62% to 45% with abnormal GLS (-14%), and she has had left chest wall radiotherapy. Standard R-CHOP (300 mg/m2 more, about 540 mg/m2 in total) would exceed the usual cumulative ceiling of roughly 450-550 mg/m2 in a patient with established cardiotoxicity. Pola-R-CHP also contains doxorubicin and is excluded for the same reason. Dexrazoxane or dose reduction does not make the remaining anthracycline acceptable at this LVEF. Polatuzumab is the only agent with randomized benefit in DLBCL that is not cardiotoxic, and it is the closest analogue of the POLARIX regimen. Vincristine is omitted, which also avoids neuropathy. Evidence for anthracycline-free regimens is limited and mostly non-randomized, so verify the current NCCN version and the available trials. If polatuzumab is unavailable, the alternative is R-CEOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, etoposide, vincristine, prednisone). I would not use ibrutinib (atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and it is designed around an anthracycline backbone), DA-EPOCH-R (contains doxorubicin), or R-GemOx (weaker). Start cycle 1 within about 1-2 weeks, once GDMT is started and cardiology has reviewed; do not wait for LVEF recovery. Radiotherapy is not planned for PET-negative disease; if PET-positive residual disease remains, discuss with radiation oncology, since an axillary field overlaps the prior left breast field. Clinical trial referral is strongly encouraged. What would change this plan: (1) repeat FISH confirms a MYC plus BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement, which would prompt a discussion of DA-EPOCH-R or a trial with cardiology-approved anthracycline exposure; (2) LVEF below about 40% or new heart failure, which would mean treating heart failure first and deferring chemotherapy; (3) interim PET showing no metabolic response, which would prompt re-biopsy and a change of strategy.
answer.cns_risk: CNS relapse risk is intermediate by my estimate. The CNS-IPI points she has are stage III and elevated LDH; age, performance status, and kidney and adrenal involvement do not contribute. Verify the exact point total against the published score. She has no testicular, breast, paranasal sinus, kidney, adrenal or marrow involvement, and she is not double-hit. The only lymphoid site beyond nodes is the spleen. Routine CNS prophylaxis (intrathecal or high-dose methotrexate) is therefore not indicated, and no proven benefit outweighs its toxicity in this setting. Neurological exam is normal, so no brain MRI or lumbar puncture is needed unless symptoms develop. I would revisit this if repeat pathology or imaging changes the risk category, or if she develops neurological or ocular symptoms.
answer.response_assessment: Baseline FDG PET-CT (2026-09-04) is Deauville 5 throughout (liver SUVmax 2.7; mediastinal blood pool 1.9). Key lesions: mesenteric conglomerate 7.5 x 5.1 cm (SUVmax 22.3, largest); para-aortic nodes up to 3.0 cm (SUVmax 16.9); mediastinal nodes up to 2.9 cm (SUVmax 15.4); left axillary nodes up to 2.2 cm (SUVmax 17.8); splenic nodules up to 2.1 cm (SUVmax 16.2); spleen 12.8 cm. Repeat PET-CT with the same scanner and SUV method after cycle 2 (interim) and after cycle 6 (end of treatment), with Lugano 2014 Deauville scoring. Clinical response is assessed at each cycle: fever, night sweats, weight, axillary node, spleen size, LDH and CBC. Interpretation: at interim, Deauville 1-3 means continue; Deauville 4-5 with a clear reduction means continue, since the regimen is anthracycline-free and the interim value is not validated for it; Deauville 4-5 with no meaningful reduction or any new lesion means early failure, so re-biopsy and change strategy (trial or salvage). At end of treatment, Deauville 1-3 is a complete metabolic response: no consolidation radiotherapy and surveillance only. Deauville 4-5 at end of treatment needs biopsy to confirm before salvage. Cardiac response: repeat echocardiogram with biplane LVEF and GLS at end of treatment and sooner for symptoms; cardiology to set the surveillance schedule. Breast surveillance continues on its usual schedule.
answer.pretreatment_workup: Already done: diagnostic pathology with IHC and FISH; flow cytometry; bone marrow negative; FDG PET-CT; echocardiogram; HIV and HCV negative; HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs all nonreactive, so no HBV reactivation prophylaxis is needed, but she is not immune and should be vaccinated after treatment. CMP is normal; LDH 510 (2.3 times ULN); uric acid 5.8; beta-2 microglobulin 2.9. Still needed before cycle 1: (1) Cardiology assessment with ECG, high-sensitivity troponin, NT-proBNP, and a repeat biplane echocardiogram with GLS, plus cardiac MRI if available. An ischemia evaluation is warranted given prior left chest radiotherapy and hypertension. (2) Current CBC with differential, CMP, magnesium, phosphate, uric acid and LDH; the last full set is from 2026-09-01. (3) Quantitative IgG, IgA and IgM before rituximab; TSH, HbA1c, lipids; urinalysis. (4) Menopausal status and pregnancy test if not confirmed postmenopausal. (5) Baseline neuropathy exam. (6) Vaccinations (inactivated influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal) before cycle 1 if they can be given without delay. (7) TLS prophylaxis: risk is at least intermediate given LDH 2.3 times ULN and a 7.5 cm mass; allopurinol with cautious hydration; check uric acid, potassium, phosphate and creatinine at 24, 48 and 72 hours. (8) Peripheral IV access is adequate for this regimen; port placement is not required.
answer.supportive_care: Cardiac, start now and do not wait for chemotherapy: an ACE inhibitor (or ARB) and carvedilol, targeting BP below 130/80. Amlodipine can be stopped or replaced once BP is controlled. Add an SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin) once she is stable; hold it on days of poor oral intake. Check potassium and creatinine 1-2 weeks after starting the ACE inhibitor. Monitor weight and fluid status each cycle. Hold antihypertensives on the morning of rituximab infusions, per labeling. Hydration for cyclophosphamide should be oral and moderate, with IV fluid limited because of LVEF 45%. Infection: PJP prophylaxis with TMP-SMX during prednisone cycles. Because she is on an ACE inhibitor, check potassium closely, or use atovaquone if potassium rises. Fever: any temperature of 38.0 C or higher needs prompt evaluation with cultures and a neutropenia assessment; acetaminophen is acceptable and NSAIDs should be avoided. Primary G-CSF is not routinely needed for Pola-R-CP; reassess if neutropenia or infection occurs. HBV prophylaxis not needed. Antiemesis: 5-HT3 antagonist with dexamethasone (the prednisone course also contributes). Anemia (Hb 11.4): transfuse for Hb below 8 given her cardiac disease. Pola-related neuropathy and diarrhea should be monitored. TLS prophylaxis as above. Bone health: continue calcium and vitamin D; DEXA due 2027; continue anastrozole. Vaccines: inactivated only; no live vaccines.
answer.fitness_and_goals: ECOG 1, age 59, independent in daily activities, NYHA class I, normal renal and hepatic function. She is fit for curative-intent immunochemotherapy, but not for anthracyclines. The cardiac issue is manageable with guideline therapy and an anthracycline-free regimen. Her goal is cure and a return to full-time school library work. Six 21-day cycles take about 4-5 months. She can expect reduced hours during treatment, though many people work between cycles; a work letter and a graded return will help. Prognosis should be discussed honestly: a good chance of remission, cure not assured, and PET results will guide the next steps. Her husband should be included in the discussion, and advance care planning and a healthcare proxy should be documented. Anastrozole: continue to the planned end of 10 years (November 2026). It has no meaningful interaction with Pola-R-CP and remains indicated for her ER-positive breast cancer. The lymphoma diagnosis is not a reason to stop it. The breast oncology team should confirm the end date. If the lymphoma relapses, options include CAR-T (requires cardiac clearance), bispecific antibodies, or anthracycline-free salvage such as R-GDP, R-ICE or polatuzumab-BR. Anthracyclines should be avoided in any further line of therapy.
missing_information: Cardiology evaluation results: ECG, high-sensitivity troponin, NT-proBNP, biplane LVEF and GLS repeat echo, cardiac MRI if available, and ischemia assessment (prior left chest radiotherapy and hypertension). The 2016 study did not measure GLS, so the strain decline cannot be trended from baseline.
Current laboratory values: the last CBC, CMP, LDH and uric acid are from 2026-09-01. Quantitative immunoglobulins, TSH, HbA1c, lipids, urinalysis, magnesium and phosphate are not in the chart.
Menopausal status and pregnancy test status are not documented.
Vaccination history and any HBV immunity plan (HBsAb is nonreactive).
No infection workup (cultures, urinalysis, chest imaging) is documented for the febrile episodes; infection needs to be excluded before cycle 1.
Confirmation of the 240 mg/m2 cumulative doxorubicin dose from the 2016 treatment records; the chart summary states it but does not include the source.
Repeat FISH or alternative MYC/BCL2/BCL6 testing if the diagnosis is in doubt; a confirmed double-hit result would change the plan.
Optional genotyping (TP53, MYD88 L265P, CD79B) and PET images: the baseline Deauville scores are inferred from the written report and have not been reviewed on the images.
Polatuzumab access and insurance authorization, clinical trial eligibility, and the patient's own informed preference after counseling.
Input from breast oncology on the anastrozole end date and mammography schedule.
Baseline spirometry and DLCO (optional, given the prior radiation-associated lung change).

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a non-germinal-center (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm.
The response notes that Hans non-GCB is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not equivalent to molecular ABC cell-of-origin by gene-expression profiling.
The response states the left axillary node is lymphoma and not recurrent breast carcinoma (cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 negative).
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage III (nodes on both sides of the diaphragm with splenic involvement).
The response explains that the spleen is lymphatic tissue (a nodal site), so splenic nodules do not make the disease stage IV, and that there is no non-lymphatic extranodal or marrow involvement.
The response notes B symptoms (documented fevers >38 C and drenching night sweats).
The response notes the 7.5 cm mass is below the 10 cm Lugano bulk threshold, acknowledging that bulk definitions vary (some trials use 7.5 cm).
The response stages this patient as stage IV (e.g. by counting splenic involvement as extranodal disease).
The response classifies the lymphoma as double-expressor by IHC (MYC 45% >=40%, BCL2 70% >=50%) but NOT double-hit (FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R (or another intensified regimen) on the basis of double-expressor biology.
The response calculates IPI as 2 (low-intermediate risk): elevated LDH and stage III; age 59, ECOG 1 and no extranodal sites (spleen is not counted as extranodal) score zero.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 2 (intermediate risk).
The response states that routine CNS prophylaxis is not indicated (CNS-IPI 2, no kidney/adrenal, testicular or breast involvement).
The response mandates CNS prophylaxis (high-dose methotrexate or intrathecal therapy) for this patient.

The response recognizes anthracycline-related cardiac risk (prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest radiotherapy, LVEF fall from 62% to 45%, i.e. cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction) and does NOT plan standard full-dose doxorubicin (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP) without first addressing cardiac function.

The response recommends standard R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP (full-dose doxorubicin) without conditioning it on the reduced LVEF / prior anthracycline exposure (e.g. without cardio-oncology clearance, a cardioprotective modification, or a non-anthracycline alternative).
The response requests urgent cardio-oncology (or cardiology) evaluation before starting therapy.
The response starts or optimizes guideline-directed cardioprotective therapy: an ACE inhibitor/ARB (or ARNI) plus a beta-blocker (e.g. carvedilol), for example replacing amlodipine.

The response recommends a curative-intent anthracycline-free or anthracycline-modified regimen, e.g. R-CEOP (etoposide in place of doxorubicin) or R-GCVP; R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or dexrazoxane is acceptable only if conditioned on cardio-oncology judging it safe.
The response acknowledges that anthracycline-free regimens likely have lower efficacy than anthracycline-based therapy.
The response plans serial cardiac monitoring during therapy: repeat LVEF/GLS imaging plus troponin and/or natriuretic peptide (BNP/NT-proBNP).
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.
The response assesses tumor lysis risk as low-intermediate (normal creatinine and uric acid, LDH ~2x ULN) and gives allopurinol with hydration for cycle 1.
The response recommends (or reasonably considers) primary G-CSF support with each cycle.
The response addresses the ongoing anastrozole: continuing it is acceptable (no meaningful interaction), or holding it in coordination with breast oncology is also acceptable.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) before rituximab.
The response judges the patient fit for curative-intent therapy (ECOG 1, normal organ function apart from the LVEF) and acknowledges her goal of cure.
The response lists the cause of the LVEF decline / cardio-oncology work-up as missing (e.g. ischemic evaluation given prior left chest radiotherapy, cardiac MRI, baseline troponin and NT-proBNP).
